title: Debounced Async Username Check
prompt:
Validate that a username is available, debouncing the request and ignoring stale results. **Requirements:** 1. Import `useEffect`, `useState`, and `ChangeEvent` from `react`. 2. Define and export `type CheckState = 'idle' | 'checking' | 'available' | 'taken'`. 3. Export a function component `UsernameCheck({ check }: { check: (name: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise })` -- `check` resolves to `true` if the name is available. 4. Inside the component: - Hold `name: string` and `state: CheckState`. - When `name.length < 3`, state must be `'idle'`. - Otherwise, after a 300ms debounce, set state to `'checking'`, call `check(name, signal)` with an `AbortController` signal, and update state to `'available'` or `'taken'`. Cancel the previous timer and abort on cleanup. 5. Render an `` and a status `

` whose text is the current state.
hints: `setTimeout` returns the debounce handle; clearing it on cleanup is what makes the debounce work.
Pair the debounce with an `AbortController` so a slow response from a stale name can never overwrite the latest one.
Short-circuit when `name.length < 3` so you don't fire the network for partial input.
